articleTitle: Disney’s Free Trial, a Wrongful Death: Disney invoked a Disney+ free-trial agreement and park-ticket
summary: Disney’s Free Trial, a Wrongful Death: Disney invoked a Disney+ free-trial agreement and park-ticket terms to push a wrongful-death claim into individual arbitration rather than court. The mechanism concerned access to a courtroom, not immunity from liability; Disney subsequently abandoned arbitration, and the plaintiff later voluntarily dismissed the lawsuit. Receipts: The court-filed Disney Terms of Use required that “any dispute between you and us, except for small claims, is subject to a class action waiver and must be resolved by individual binding arbitration.”

systemMechanisms.mechanism: Capture agreement during an ordinary streaming signup.
systemMechanisms.operation: Disney said account creation required clicking “Agree & Continue” beside a hyperlink to the Subscriber Agreement. That agreement also referred users to the broader Disney Terms of Use.​
systemMechanisms.plainEnglish: A click made to access entertainment became evidence Disney later offered in a dispute about a fatal restaurant visit.
systemMechanisms.disputedPoint: Piccolo’s lawyers argued that the broader Terms of Use were linked inside another linked document, rather than conspicuously presented on the registration screen.

systemMechanisms.mechanism: Connect the streaming account to other Disney businesses.
systemMechanisms.operation: Section 7 of the broader Terms of Use addressed disputes involving The Walt Disney Company or its affiliates and defined covered disputes by reference to Disney Services or the agreement, including claims in contract, tort, warranty, statute, regulation or another legal or equitable basis.​
systemMechanisms.plainEnglish: Disney sought to make the account’s legal terms travel across its corporate family.
systemMechanisms.scopeCaution: The clause was broad but not literally unlimited: its text retained a connection to Disney Services or the agreement. Disney argued that the complaint’s reliance on its website supplied that connection.

systemMechanisms.mechanism: Add the park-ticket transaction as another contractual connection.
systemMechanisms.operation: Disney cited Piccolo’s acceptance of My Disney Experience terms, his ticket purchase and his registration of Tangsuan as a guest. The quoted terms purported to cover the account holder and people for whom the holder secured or managed benefits, and stated that they applied in addition to the Disney Terms of Use.
systemMechanisms.plainEnglish: Disney did not rely solely on a streaming trial. It also used the family’s vacation-planning transactions to argue that the broader terms governed.

systemMechanisms.mechanism: Apply the account holder’s agreement to an estate’s wrongful-death action.
systemMechanisms.operation: Disney asked to compel Piccolo, acting as personal representative, to arbitrate all claims against Disney. The opposition distinguished Piccolo personally from the estate and invoked Fla. Stat. § 768.20, arguing that his individual agreements could not bind his wife’s estate.​
systemMechanisms.plainEnglish: The contested leap was from a husband’s personal clicks to the legal rights asserted after his wife’s death.

systemMechanisms.mechanism: Ask an arbitrator to decide whether arbitration applies.
systemMechanisms.operation: Disney relied on a delegation clause giving an arbitrator exclusive authority over interpretation, applicability, enforceability and arbitrability. The plaintiff argued that the court first had to determine whether the relevant agreement existed at all.​
systemMechanisms.plainEnglish: Disney wanted even much of the argument about the proper forum decided inside arbitration.

systemMechanisms.mechanism: Replace courtroom adjudication with individual arbitration.
systemMechanisms.operation: The court-filed terms required attempted informal resolution for sixty (60) days before commencing arbitration, preserved eligible small-claims proceedings, excluded disputes over ownership or enforcement of intellectual-property rights, and otherwise specified individual JAMS arbitration under its Streamlined Arbitration Rules and Procedures. They waived class proceedings and described only limited appeal rights.
systemMechanisms.plainEnglish: The central change was the decision-maker and procedure: an arbitrator instead of a judge or jury deciding the merits. The terms expressly permitted individual damages and declaratory or injunctive relief; arbitration was not automatic immunity.

systemMechanisms.mechanism: Pause the lawsuit while arbitration proceeds.
systemMechanisms.operation: Disney invoked 9 U.S.C. § 3 to request a stay of the claims against it. It also sought a discretionary stay of the restaurant claims, arguing that overlapping facts could produce inconsistent decisions.
systemMechanisms.plainEnglish: Success could have redirected the Disney claims and delayed the related court case against the restaurant. That was requested relief, not an outcome Disney obtained.

coreControversy.criticismOrAlarm: Unregulated shadow banking float without FDIC protection
coreControversy.regulatoryOrHistoricalPrecedent: Exempt from reserve ratios and Dodd-Frank requirements
